text:
sam: Heads-up — customer reported duplicated token consumption when a WS client stalls mid-stream and then reconnects. Looks like we charge for the resumed session plus a new session.
li: Which customer / which route? can you paste the session id? :thinking_face:
sam: tenant=acme-inc, route=/v1/stream/chat, session=aa3f9c4b. Kibana trace: https://kibana.internal/redwood/trace/aa3f9c4b. Observed two billing events ~3s apart.
kevin: that route has priority routing enabled and a soft ratecap. Might be hitting the ratecap logic that duplicates accept vs resume accounting.
nora: is this the orphaned-ack-window we talked about during the routing refactor? where the proxy marks the old lease dead but the backend still bills resume tokens?
sam: Yep. My quick read: client stalls (network hiccup), proxy drops socket but doesn't send final ledger ack; client reconnects and gets a new lease. Both sessions incur token delta for the same in-flight chunk.
li: any server logs showing ack mismatch? snippet:
```
[I] 2026-03-21T18:12:01Z session aa3f9c4b recv chunk id=217 acked=false
[I] 2026-03-21T18:12:04Z proxy drop conn id=xyz
[I] 2026-03-21T18:12:05Z session reconnect new_id=bb7f... charge tokens=120
[I] 2026-03-21T18:12:06Z ledger charge old_id=aa3f9c4b tokens=120
```
nora: so ledger processes the old session's delayed commit after the new session already started. order-of-ops bug.
kevin: sounds like we need idempotency on the charge side keyed by (tenant, stream_chunk_id) and a short GC window where duplicate charges are collapsed.
sam: agreed. Also the console telemetry shows two per-route spikes. UX issue: customers see double cost for a single user experience. We should annotate billing events as "possible-duplicate" in console when they fall within the orphan window.
li: alternative quick mitigation: on reconnect, return a resume token that references the previous in-flight chunk id and instruct client to ack/skip. But clients vary — can't rely on them.
kevin: infra idea: when we see a late charge for session X and there's an active session Y for same tenant+chunk, treat the late charge as a no-op and emit a reconciliation event. That needs atomic check in ledger. Could be done by adding `charged_chunk_ids` set per-tenant with short TTL.
nora: we'll need a migration plan. ledger currently appends charges; making it idempotent is non-trivial.
sam: for immediate triage: roll a canary that returns a special header `x-resume-safe: true/false` from proxy so the console can flag these routes. Low-risk UI change while infra works the ledger change.
kevin: who will own the ledger change? @nora? this touches quota accounting and reserved capacity.
nora: I can take it but need 2 days to design API + test harness for concurrency. I'll pair with @kevin for atomic updates.
li: I'll add a console annotation patch to surface suspected duplicates and a dashboard panel showing "suspected duplicate charge rate" (count of charges within 10s for same chunk id). Quick PR today.
sam: can we add an alert: when suspected duplicates > 0.5% of route volume for a tenant in 5m window, page oncall? This is revenue-critical.
deploy-bot: deploy queued by li for branch `console/duplicate-flag` to canary-3 (eta ~ 12m)
kevin: ops note — watch queue depth on ledger writes when we add dedupe set; might need to shard the set by tenant hash.
nora: plan: (1) console flag + dashboard (li) — 24h, (2) proxy header + canary (sam) — 48h, (3) ledger idempotency + tests (nora+kevin) — 2w. I'll write ADR and timeline.
sam: thanks. can everyone drop their relevant traces here so we can attach to the ADR? also add any unit tests that simulate stall+reconnect.
li: attaching quick Sysdig view and a small reproducer using `websocat` in the thread.

--- reproducer ---
```
# simulate stall
websocat ws://ingest.redwood/v1/stream/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer x' 
# send large prompt, then sleep on client to force stall
```

sam: moving to ow-queue. tagging @oncall for visibility. :bell:
nora: noted. I'll kick off the ADR draft.
kevin: thanks all. follow-up sync in sprint planning tomorrow.
